parsed.explanation: Section 379 makes male-assigned gender presentation a criminal offence (up to three months), a universal exposure for visibly trans women, while security forces are documented harassing, arresting, detaining, torturing and beating LGBTQI+ people (2018–2022). No hate-crime or anti-discrimination recourse exists, and LGBTQI+ organising has been raided and closed. The same-sex conduct law is unenforced but remains on the books; the dress provision's enforcement is not sourced. No death penalty or execution pathway is documented, and no visitor-specific border, document or healthcare evidence exists. The combination is a known appearance-based criminal exposure plus state-tolerated abuse and no remedy, but not routine visitor arrest or lethal custody. High Risk, above the severe band.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No data on entry or visa screening, passport-marker mismatches, or border questioning of trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented border rule can be rated as a separate exposure; ordinary entry remains an open question, not evidence of safety.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Section 379 criminalises a male person dressing as a woman, up to three months; security forces are reported to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ persons (2018–2022).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No hate-crime or anti-discrimination law; no LGBTQI+ support organisations.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Appearance alone can trigger police contact; once detained, documented abuse and no effective recourse raise severity.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Nationwide Section 379 and 'unnatural offence' provisions; no subnational variation. No facility or custody-placement data for trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Only oil-and-gas employment harassment protection is documented, which is irrelevant to visitor facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No geographic safe zone is documented; nationwide criminal law follows the traveller across regions.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No data on gender-affirming care, medication continuity, or hospital ward practices for trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: Care access cannot be assessed; no protective rule is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Minister stated in 2017 the government would order arrests of LGBTQ persons and detention until they procreate; official rhetoric is hostile; security-force abuse is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No general anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; no moratorium or repeal is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing licenses police targeting; the ministerial statement is not shown formalised but reinforces risk.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented specifically. Same dress and conduct laws and police-abuse reports may reach minors; no safeguards are documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent or guardian has no documented protective recourse; a minor's visible gender nonconformity carries similar appearance-based exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Security forces reported to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ persons; societal discrimination is 'widespread'; most openly LGBTQI+ citizens have fled.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime law, no anti-discrimination law, no known LGBTQI+ organisations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are a documented source of harm, not recourse; reporting violence is unlikely to produce protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No effective remedy documented; a rights group was raided in 2017, staff detained months, organisation closed; NGO Act constrains LGBTQI+ organising.
remedies_unknowns.protection: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse; no known support groups.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of independent advocacy and legal protection leaves detention or abuse without a realistic complaint channel.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A has routine arrests for presentation, months of pretrial custody, beatings, and a capital provision. The dossier's dress offence carries only up to three months, no execution is documented, and dress enforcement is not sourced. It is less severe than 0.15-A, so above it.

0.25-B has transport-police extortion, threatened arrest, overnight cells, short jail and dismissed complaints. Here there is an explicit appearance offence and documented police torture of LGBTQI+ people, but no documented routine shakedowns or visitor arrests. Comparable high-risk tier; placed just below 0.25-B.
0.35-A is border exclusion and humiliation with no imprisonment. This dossier reaches possible imprisonment under the dress law and documented police abuse, so it is materially below 0.35-A.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a directly appearance-based criminal offence (Section 379), documented state and security-force abuse of LGBTQI+ people, hostile official rhetoric, and no hate-crime, anti-discrimination or civil-society recourse. The same-sex conduct law is unenforced on the record, and no visitor-specific border, document, care or facility practice is documented; those are open questions, not protections. The dress offence creates universal exposure for visibly trans women, but no routine visitor arrest or execution pathway is shown. This sits in High Risk, below 0.25-B's routine shakedown tier and well above the severe 0.15 anchors.
